summary: Explains that delegated tasks still run in parallel forks, so many hosts updating one file on a delegated host can overwrite each other. Solutions: `run_once: true` with a loop over `ansible_play_hosts_all`, an intermediate play with `serial: 1`, or `throttle: 1`.
questions: Why do my hosts overwrite each other when updating one file on localhost with delegate_to?
How do I serialize a delegated lineinfile task?
What's the easiest way to make a delegated task run one host at a time?

answer_card.title: Concurrency with delegated tasks
answer_card.answer_md:
Delegation doesn't change parallel execution: tasks still run in parallel forks (default 5) and nothing protects against multiple forks writing the same file. Updating one file on one delegated host with `copy`, `template`, or `lineinfile` can therefore clobber itself.

Fixes:
```yaml
- name: Loop over hosts once
  lineinfile: "<options here>"
  run_once: true
  loop: '{{ ansible_play_hosts_all }}'
```
or use an intermediate play with `serial: 1`, or `throttle: 1` on the task.
